verses.text: Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jehoram became king after him.
Jehoram had brothers, the other sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
Their father had given them many gifts of silver, gold, and valuable things, and walled towns in Judah. But he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the oldest son.
When Jehoram had taken over his father's kingdom and made his power secure, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the leaders of Israel too.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for eight years in Jerusalem.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, just as Ahab's family had done, because he was married to Ahab's daughter. He did evil in the LORD's eyes.
But the LORD did not want to destroy David's family, because of the covenant he had made with David. He had promised to keep a lamp burning for David and his descendants forever.
While Jehoram was king, Edom rebelled against Judah and chose its own king.
So Jehoram went there with his commanders and all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him, but he got up at night and attacked them and their chariot commanders.
So Edom has been free from Judah's rule to this day. At the same time the town of Libnah also rebelled against him, because he had left the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
He also built hilltop shrines in the hills of Judah. He led the people of Jerusalem to be unfaithful to God, like a woman selling her body, and he led Judah astray.
Then a letter came to Jehoram from the prophet Elijah. It said, "The LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: 'You have not followed the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or of Asa king of Judah.

Instead you have followed the ways of the kings of Israel. You have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem to be unfaithful to me, just as Ahab's family did. You also murdered your own brothers, your father's sons, who were better than you.
So now the LORD is about to strike your people with a terrible disaster, including your children, your wives, and everything you own.
You yourself will become very sick with a disease of your bowels. Day after day it will get worse until your bowels come out.'"
The LORD stirred up the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to attack Jehoram.
They attacked Judah, broke in, and carried off everything they found in the king's palace, along with his sons and his wives. Only Jehoahaz, his youngest son, was left.
After all this, the LORD struck Jehoram with a disease of the bowels that could not be cured.
After about two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in terrible pain. His people did not light a fire to honor him, as they had done for his ancestors.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years. No one was sad when he died. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
